_doc: src/shared/geofence.ts and the configurable geofence of the browser simulator (tool 9 of Lote 1; the simulator is NOT PX4, and the own fence of PX4, GF_*, does not reach the client). `validate`: validateFence(cfg, state) at its borders; `out` is "ok" or the error `code` (the Spanish `detail` is not part of the contract except in the replies of `scenarios`). The in-flight rule applies only when armed and not landed: radius >= horizontal distance + 5 m and ceiling >= height + 2 m (within 1e-9), otherwise it is refused and nothing moves. `status`: fenceMargins (horizontal = radius - distance, vertical = ceiling - height, min of both, m; negative = outside) and fenceStatus ("hit" at <= 0.05 m, "near" under 5 m, else "ok"). `storage`: parseFence of the text kept under twinsight.sim.fence.v1 (anything invalid gives the defaults). `scenarios` are scripts run on a fresh createSim(22) in the format of flightsim.json (see its _doc) plus the op `config` (setSimConfig with the partial `cfg`; the reply { reply: "config", ok, detail, event, code } is recorded, `code` only when refused); the rows list the states in `state_columns` then `frame_columns`, and `final_cfg` is the geofence at the end. The desktop port must reproduce every state number within `tolerance.state`, the frame numbers within `tolerance.frame`, the rpm within `tolerance.rpm`, the margins within `tolerance.margin` and every string, flag, code and reply text exactly.
